scope: Complete surviving Asheville Masonic Temple/Scottish Rite Cathedral at80Broadway: west front portion and intrinsic connected east hall represented by touching native ways490235622/490235623, pressed redbrick three full floors over dark granite basement, pale limestone/greybrick bands and dressed recessed sash, two-story Broadway portico with four unfluted Ionic columns in two pairs and genuinely recessed open upper balcony/loggia, lower stone balustrade and upper metal rail, arched recessed closed entry/own steps, broad bracketed cornice and red-tile front hip roof/brick chimney, taller rear hall gable roof and north Woodfin shaped brick parapet with three tall blind thermal-arch recesses above small sash. Exclude separate neighboring buildings, sidewalk/roads/signals/trees/people/cars, lettering/Masonic artwork and interiors.

quallaSearch.notes: Qualla-first inventory completed. Three exact already-cleared published WarrenLeMayCC0exterior originals inspected:4032x3024front/4032x3024wide/3024x4032oblique. Native Commons SHA1, source author and explicit cc-zero record matched. Wide oblique shows front hipped roof and connected taller gable hall with Woodfin blind thermal arch; primary historic district text independently confirms hip-front/gable-hall and paired Ionic Broadway portico. Both touching map polygons belong to this complete structure; mapped seam is not an excuse to omit its rear hall. Entryway floor mosaic viewed but unused; portrait/old different temple/lamps/artwork/interiors and uncertain media excluded. No supplemental images, copied pixels or generatedbitmap.
